title: Implement broker fee activity ingestion and account equity reconciliation reports
acceptance_criteria: mike_trade/reporting/fees.py defines FeeStatus with exactly the values CONFIRMED, ESTIMATED and UNAVAILABLE, plus activity normalization, classification and idempotent ingestion functions
Re-ingesting an identical broker activity id produces no additional persisted record or event, as demonstrated by a test
A fee is reported CONFIRMED only when a broker activity links it to the order; otherwise it is ESTIMATED with an estimated label or UNAVAILABLE, and no code path accepts an operator-supplied fee file
Normalized activity records keep only allowlisted fields; tests assert that secret-like keys, full account identifiers and unknown raw payload fields are absent

accounting.py reports cash, buying power, authorized budget, symbol commitment, realized gross, fees by status, net realized, unrealized (with mark source/as-of/stale), external flows and income as separate Decimal fields
The reconciliation identity yields residual 0 and reconciled=true on a consistent fixture, and a nonzero residual with reconciled=false on an inconsistent fixture
Deposits and withdrawals change equity and external_flows but never realized or unrealized trading P&L, as demonstrated by a test
Day and week periods use America/New_York session boundaries, while stored and returned timestamps are timezone-aware UTC
Requests spanning multiple accounts or modes are rejected, and SHADOW fees are always labeled ESTIMATED
tests/unit/test_reporting_reconciliation.py contains passing positive and negative tests and uses no network access or broker credentials
forbidden_changes: add any manual or hand-loaded fee file import path
fabricate per-order fees or report estimated fees as confirmed
persist raw unfiltered provider payloads, secrets or full account identifiers
write to the database outside the existing single authoritative writer path
combine balances or P&L across accounts, modes or scenarios
use float for money, quantity or fee values
access broker credentials, call real broker endpoints, or create broker orders
run broad test suites or backtests
